chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Qalanisi, from Ahmad ibn al-Fadl, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Fazara, from Anas or Haysam ibn al-Bara', from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'The burglar enters upon me in my house intending [to take] my life and my wealth.' He said, 'Kill him, and I will call Allah and whoever hears me as witness that his blood is upon my neck.'

He said, 'I said, 'May Allah make you well! So where is the sign of this matter?' He said, 'Do you see [the dawn] from concealment?' I said, 'No.' He said, 'So our matter, when it comes, will be clearer than the break of dawn.'

He said, 'Then he said, 'Engaging with a mountain by fingernail is easier than engaging with a kingdom whose consumption has not yet expired. Therefore, fear Allah, Blessed and High, and do not kill yourselves for the unjust ones.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on killing a burglar in Shia jurisprudence and what is the sign of the Imam's appearance?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the concept of *qatl al-liss* (killing the burglar) is clarified not merely as self-defense but as a right where the killer bears no blood-guilt, provided the intent was lethal or for wealth. The Imam further links this legal ruling to the eschatological sign of the Mahdi’s rise, describing it as unmistakably clear as the dawn, while concluding with a practical political warning against serving unjust rulers, which leads to spiritual and physical ruin.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad Al Qalanasy, from Ahmad Bin Al Fazl, from Abdullah Bin Jabala, from Fazara, from Ans, or Haysam Bin Al Bara’a, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The burglar entered upon me in my house intending (killing) me and (taking) my wealth’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So kill him, for I<sup>asws</sup> keep Allah<sup>azwj</sup> as a Witness along with the one who hears me<sup>asws</sup>, that his blood is upon my neck’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘I said, ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Keep you<sup>asws</sup> well! So where is the sign of this matter (Al-Qaim<sup>asws</sup>)?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do you see the morning from concealment?’ I said, ‘No’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So, our<sup>asws</sup> matter, when it would be, would be clearer than the break of dawn in the morning’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Achievement by engaging with a mountain is easier than engaging with a kingdom whose consumption is yet to expire. Therefore, fear Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High, and do not kill yourselves for the unjust ones’.
